title: BigBrain cortical laminar boundaries

space.name: BigBrain cortical laminar boundaries original surface coordinates
space.reference: Original self-contained GIfTI point arrays and triangle arrays in the BigBrain histological release. Embedded identity coordinate matrices are recorded.
space.correspondence: Surfaces within this package share the author release coordinate convention. Separate datasets retain their own source spaces and definitions.
space.unit_basis: The BigBrain histological release and associated source paper describe surface distances and morphometry in millimeters. Original coordinates are retained with metric scale 1.0; no shrinkage correction is added.

sources.title: BigBrain cortical laminar boundaries
sources.citation: Wagstyl K et al. BigBrain 3D atlas of cortical layers: Cortical and laminar thickness gradients diverge in sensory and motor cortices. PLoS Biology 18:e3000678 (2020). doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.3000678. BigBrain foundation: Amunts K et al. Science 340:1472-1475 (2013), doi:10.1126/science.1235381. Original contributors: https://ftp.bigbrainproject.org/bigbrain-ftp/Credits.txt.

model_evidence: Original histology-derived cortical boundary surfaces published by Wagstyl et al.; source computational inference in the normal BigBrain specimen.
model_notes: Wagstyl et al. infer six cortical layers from histological profiles in a single BigBrain specimen. The source applies its own surface processing; these exact released vertices and triangles are preserved.
The source-defined layer boundaries can be difficult to distinguish in some cortical regions. Layer IV and transitions between adjacent layers have region-dependent uncertainty.
The study identifies a histological layer VI / white matter boundary that differs from an intensity-gradient surface. Keep the explicit boundary definition when comparing with MRI-derived cortex.
Original point order, shared mesh topology and source filenames are retained. Native surface distance is distinct from corrected in-vivo cortical thickness.
scope_notes: One source-designated normal adult postmortem specimen; source computational processing and reconstructed boundaries are retained.
Native source surfaces support spatial observation. Layer and subfield definitions remain specific to their source method.

teaching_sequences.title: Left cortical boundary sequence
teaching_sequences.instruction: Inspect the pial surface, then the successive layer boundaries and the layer VI / white matter boundary. Use transparency and the prepared cutaway to follow the nested surfaces through folds.
teaching_sequences.evidence_limit: Source-author inferred boundaries from histology; the original anatomical processing is retained.
teaching_sequences.step_prompt: Trace the selected supplied surface and describe its relationship to the other visible source components.
teaching_sequences.step_question: Which source component is selected, and how does its supplied extent relate to the visible neighboring surfaces?
